input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: Calling `.strip()` also removes intentional leading and trailing whitespace from the prompt, even when it contains no ANSI codes.
- rationale: When stdout does not support ANSI, a prompt such as `"Name: "` becomes `"Name:"`, and prompts with leading newlines or indentation lose that formatting. The branch should remove ANSI sequences while preserving the prompt's whitespace; otherwise displayed or captured prompts change beyond color removal.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism: `.strip()` applied after ANSI removal on the non-color path drops the prompt's trailing whitespace, turning 'Name: ' into 'Name:'. It ties this to the case where stdout lacks ANSI support, which is the labeled defect.
